subject: Dedicated capacity: billing structure options & PO flow
messages:
From: Jared Liu <jared.liu@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Martins <sophie.martins@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring Dedicated capacity options for inference workloads

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a quick internal sizing model and it looks like we'll need ~16-20 A100-equivalent GPUs to meet peak throughput for our inference pipelines, with spiky traffic during batch windows.

Before we get legal/finance involved, procurement asked for a clear breakdown of the billing options you support for Dedicated: monthly prepay vs. annual prepay, how true-ups work if we exceed committed throughput, whether we can submit a single PO that covers the commit and later true-ups, and the net terms you typically accept (Net 30/60). Also: what discounts are available for a 12 or 24-month commit, and how throughput guarantees are expressed in the contract.

Can you share a concise options matrix and an example invoice/PO flow? Sophie (cc) will coordinate procurement.

Thanks,
Jared
Jared Liu
Head of Platform
Acme Analytics
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Jared Liu <jared.liu@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Sophie Martins <sophie.martins@acmeanalytics.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring Dedicated capacity options for inference workloads

Hi Jared / Sophie,

Appreciate the details — this is exactly the right set of questions to bring to procurement. I've attached our current Dedicated_Pricing_Tiers_v3.pdf which lays out three packaging options:

- Option A: Monthly prepay (1-month commitment renewed monthly). No long-term discount; flexible scale but limited deep discount. Monthly invoices, Net 30. True-ups billed monthly if usage > commit.
- Option B: 12-month prepay (annual upfront or monthly invoiced with an annual commit). 15% discount off list for 12-month, Net 30/Net 45 negotiable. True-ups: quarterly true-up with proration for partial months. SLA: 99.9% regional uptime and committed throughput target; credits for breaches.
- Option C: 24-month prepay (annual upfront strongly preferred for max discount). 25% discount, Net 45 standard. True-ups: semi-annual true-up; capability to reserve burst capacity (pay-as-you-go for bursts above commit). Higher SLA and capacity prioritization.

Key PO/invoice flows:
- Single PO can cover the committed reservation for the contract term. True-ups are typically invoiced separately (monthly/quarterly) unless you want a single pooled PO that we draw down against; that requires billing ops coordination and is doable for enterprise procurement.
- We accept PO-based purchases and can do Net 30, Net 45, or Net 60 with an approved credit check.

I'll loop in Rishi to confirm margin room for a bespoke discount if you want to push beyond the published tiers. Can you share the projected monthly spend band (or an expected annual committed $ number) so we can propose an exact discount and final PO flow for legal?

I'm also attaching an example PO template (ACME_PO_Template.pdf) we often get back so procurement has a reference.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Sophie Martins <sophie.martins@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Jared Liu <jared.liu@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Oct 2025 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring Dedicated capacity options for inference workloads

Thanks Aisha — helpful summary.

Projected annual spend for the initial 12 months is in the $1.1M - $1.4M range depending on burst usage; baseline steady-state expected at ~$85k/month. Procurement prefers 12-month with annual prepay if the discount gets to ~18%+. They will accept Net 45 or Net 60 with approval.

A few clarifying questions so we can present to legal:
- If we pick Option B with annual prepay but increase pool size mid-year, how are credits/charges handled?
- For true-ups, does Redwood bill measured token usage or provisioned throughput? We want to avoid surprises from caching/burst anomalies.
- Can the SLA throughput target be expressed as a per-minute p99 latency for a stated QPS for our main model?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Sophie
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Exploring Dedicated capacity options for inference workloads

Aisha — copied Connor (sales engineering) for sizing guarantees and ops billing notes. Notes for negotiation:

- Given projected $1.1M-$1.4M ARR, we have room beyond standard 15% for 12-month; propose 18% off list with annual prepay upfront or 17% with invoiced monthly but with an annual commit. If they want 24-mo, we can go to 26% with a 12-month notice clause for scale changes.
- True-up model: we prefer billing measured usage (tokens + reserved concurrency units) for fairness. For committed pools, we measure provisioned GPU-hours by the reservation and bill true-ups based on provisioned increments (not per-token) to avoid noisy token accounting. Ops can do a hybrid: reserve baseline GPUs and bill overage as usage hours.
- PO flow: we can accept a single PO for the commit; true-ups invoiced separately by default. If they want a pooled PO, finance needs the PO to include a spend bucket and us to submit monthly drawdown statements. That requires a billing SLA addendum and 2-week lead time.
- SLA throughput guarantee: sales engineering can commit to p99 tail latency for a stated QPS, but must lock model revision/sequence length profile and agreed test harness (we rely on their perf test vectors).

Connor — can you draft suggested wording for throughput SLA (p99 latency at X QPS) and a short billing addendum for pooled PO flows? Aim to keep legal redlines minimal.

Rishi
VP, Sales
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Jared Liu <jared.liu@acmeanalytics.com>, Sophie Martins <sophie.martins@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Oct 2025 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring Dedicated capacity options for inference workloads

Hi all — attaching a concise terms draft (Proposed_Dedicated_Terms_Acme_v2.docx) and a short SLA snippet here so procurement/legal can see concrete language.

SLA snippet (example):
- Committed throughput: 18 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved for Acme Analytics for the contract term.
- Performance guarantee: p99 response latency <= 450ms for the agreed QPS profile (up to 1,200 requests/min for Model-A profile, sequence length <= 1,024).
- Remedies: Service credit equal to 5% of monthly committed fee for each rolling 30-day period where p99 > 450ms, up to 30% cap per month.

Billing addendum (summary):
- Commit invoicing: Full annual commit invoiced at contract execution if annual prepay selected; otherwise invoiced monthly with annual commit clause.
- True-ups: Default monthly measured true-ups for over-provisioned hours; if pooled PO requested, true-ups billed monthly against reserved spend bucket with monthly drawdown statement.
- PO specifics: PO should reference Redwood quote #RDW-ACME-0929 and specify spend bucket name and billing contact.

Jared/Sophie — if this aligns, we can generate a final quote with exact GPU SKU counts and the 18% discount Rishi suggested. Also indicate if you want us to include a DocuSign ready contract and whether procurement requires a pre-approved supplier form.

Connor O'Brien
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Aisha / Connor / Rishi — this looks good and is close to what procurement needs.

Acme is comfortable with Option B (12-month prepay) if Redwood can confirm: 18% discount with annual prepay, Net 45, and the SLA snippet above included as an addendum. Procurement will issue a single PO covering the committed reservation (we'll use the attached PO template) and accept monthly true-ups billed against the spend bucket. Please send the final quote and a DocuSign contract; procurement will route the PO once the contract and final invoice cadence are confirmed.

I'll attach the initial PO template in my next note.

Thanks,
Sophie
